claims.citation: New York Herald, 18 July 1866, p. 1, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
The French Transatlantic Steamship Company's
steamer Pereire, Captain Duchesne, which left Brest July
7[?], at four o'clock in the afternoon, arrived at this port
early yesterday morning.
Captain Duchesne, of the Pereire, furnishes us with
telegrams containing the following advices taken from
the Paris journals of the 7th of July.
The news is one day later than the report of the Nova[cut]
Scotian published in the HERALD on Monday.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 18 July 1866, p. 4, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
By the French steamship Pereire, at this port yester-
day, we have news from Europe to the 7th of July.
The advices are only one day later, but of very great
importance, as will be seen by reference to our news and
editorial columns.
